items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I think Mr. Johnson had just left office

ctx.x: But, when you stop to think of it -- and not only that, Paul Howard, bless his heart, he explained all the benefits, you see. He would tell you, "See, when you're in the union, after you've been in the union a period of time," blah, blah, blah, so many years, 30 years or so, you don't pay dues. You're a life member. You become a life member and you get this insurance and you get the benefits. He explained all

of this, you know, he explained all of this to you, and he would take the time and go on to explain to you the advantages of being in the union. He says, 'Now, when you work you have a chance of making more money.' And he says, 'Not only that, if you don't get your money the union can protect you. The union is a protective association and they will see that you get your money.' So all this sounded very good to me. It did sound (Inaudible). And he just took the time to explain all of the advantages of being a…
Well, Paul Howard was the Secretary. Florence Cadrez, who is still around and a very lovely, wonderful woman, and she was the corresponding secretary.
